players.product: electroplating chemistry for advanced packaging & substrates (MacDermid Alpha)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Carey Dorman: record quarterly revenue, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS; organic net sales grew 13% and constant currency adjusted EBITDA increased 29% year-over-year. Electronics organic net sales grew 18%, with each of the segment's verticals up organically by double digits, led by Semiconductor at 24%; adjusted EBITDA margin excluding pass-through metals improved 50 basis points to 28.2%, driven by Electronics product mix (incremental margins in the upper end of the 30%-40% target range) and Micromax. CEO Ben Gliklich: adjusted EPS rose 22%; four straight quarters of double-digit Electronics organic sales growth; the China business grew 30% in the quarter, and the Electronics segment is on pace this year to deliver the same adjusted EBITDA the entire company generated last year.
quarterly_data.figure: organic net sales +13%; Electronics organic +18%; Semiconductor +24%; adjusted EBITDA +29% constant currency; adjusted EPS +22%; China +30%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Carey Dorman on Electronics demand: Semiconductor Solutions organic net sales grew 24% on improved order patterns for power electronics, growing momentum in thermal interface materials for high power consumption applications such as AI GPUs and CPUs, and strong demand for advanced packaging solutions from Asian OSATs (growth magnified by higher precious metals prices). Assembly Solutions grew 16% organically on high-reliability solder paste in Asia benefiting from AI power supply growth and preformed products for data center applications; engineered preforms such as TruHeight spacers, which control thermal warpage on larger chip assemblies, continued to gain traction in leading-edge applications, 'driving acceleration in our capacity expansion plans for next year'. CEO Ben Gliklich: advanced packaging sales, which sit in both the Circuitry and Semi businesses, exceeded the overall growth rate of those businesses in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Solutions +24% organic; Assembly Solutions +16% organic

quarterly_data.signal: Circuitry Solutions grew 16% organically on board metallization solutions tied to AI infrastructure and high-performance computing as customers add capacity for high-layer count architectures (CFO Carey Dorman). CFO: industry forecasts for 2026 PCB volume growth rose from around 6% in December to over 10% today. CEO Ben Gliklich: all of that growth 'and then some' comes from data center boards, while consumer electronics is quite soft; Circuitry's outperformance is more than 500 basis points relative to the expected market growth year to date, and with Circuitry up 16% while consumer electronics is down, 'you can extrapolate that we are seeing north of 20% growth' in high-end HDI circuit boards for data centers. CEO: the long-term expectation is to outperform end markets by a point or two, but with data centers the primary near-term driver, outperformance should continue to outpace that target.
quarterly_data.figure: Circuitry Solutions +16% organic; PCB volume forecast from around 6% to over 10%; outperformance more than 500 basis points; north of 20% growth in data center HDI boards

quarterly_data.signal: Kuprion ActiveCopper (thermal management, power delivery and plating copper on challenging substrates): CEO Ben Gliklich said two customers, 'really high-tech, leading-edge customers' and 'two leading technology providers to the data center ecosystem' (not named), qualified ActiveCopper for their high-volume manufacturing in Q3, 'the precursor to the revenue ramp that we expect next year'. The first site is producing in Fremont, California, the second site is underway in Connecticut and plans for a third site are underway; by late 2027 / early 2028 Element expects multiple sites supplying multiple customers, on track or 'maybe even ahead' of its commitments, and the business 'is going to be contributing material EBITDA when we get into 2028, for sure.' CEO: the supply chain is not quite caught up to where Element sees demand going.
quarterly_data.figure: two customer qualifications in Q3; revenue ramp expected next year; multiple sites by late 2027 / early 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: CEO Ben Gliklich said customers are investing heavily to build capacity ahead of surging demand, and Element has built and continues to build manufacturing capacity for several high-growth product lines, including engineered preforms and critical thermal interface products, plus local Electronics laboratories in India and Southeast Asia; Southeast Asia investment meant to de-risk geopolitics two years ago 'has now become much needed additional capacity for our customers.' CFO Carey Dorman: capex was $30 million in Q3 and $83 million year to date, now expected at roughly $110 million for the year (still less than 3% of sales), accelerating in Kuprion and thermal interface materials for hyperscalers plus plant consolidation in Industrial Solutions; the projects are tied to major customer technology roadmaps.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex roughly $110 million (less than 3% of sales); Q3 capex $30 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 outlook behind the raised approximately $720 million full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance: CEO Ben Gliklich said the implied Q4 assumes a continuation of AI-driven electronics investment, normal seasonality and continued sequential acceleration at EFC, with 2026 adjusted EPS growth north of 20% at current exchange rates and stable metal prices; 'Q4 is off to a solid start'. CFO Carey Dorman: '$175 million, $176 million is a reasonable number to back into' for Q4; Q3-to-Q4 seasonal softness was around $10 million-$15 million in the last two years and the guide implies that same $15 million, reflecting holiday operating days and 'a little bit of conservatism', nothing structural in demand or pricing. Q4 cash flow should be strong but unlikely to match Q3 as capital projects ramp and stock is built for capacity expansions.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA approximately $720 million; implied Q4 $175 million-$176 million; adjusted EPS growth north of 20%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Carey Dorman on margins: excluding incentive compensation accruals (an impact of more than 100 basis points year-over-year), incremental margins were in the mid-40s% for the whole business and 50% for Electronics, driven by growth in higher-end products where fewer ecosystem competitors can meet customer needs, which he views as sustainable; Element guided 30%-40% incrementals at its Investor Day and expects the high end of that range to continue into next year.
quarterly_data.figure: incremental margins mid-40s% (Electronics 50%) excluding incentive comp accruals

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ben Gliklich on demand into 2027: no diminution or erosion in demand over the past several months; Electronics growth has come primarily from volume (apart from metal prices and Micromax); customer order forecasts and market-research industry outlooks 'have only accelerated over the course of the year', demand is more AI-driven than consumer-driven, and 'the outlook, the capital plans, remain robust into 2027.' Leading-edge technologies are still a rather small share of overall volume, so Element should participate disproportionately; sustaining this growth needs customer capacity investments to persist for several years, which customer roadmaps support ('if anything, they're supporting incremental investment relative to what they invested today'); 'the outlook for this business has only gotten better since our May investor day.' He is comfortable outlining strength exiting 2026 and well into 2027 but not prepared to talk to 2028 demand, which Kuprion should enhance.

CEO Ben Gliklich on glass core substrates: Element's circuitry portfolio has 'very solid solutions for plating on glass through glass vias', and ActiveCopper 'is also one of the leading candidates to solve that problem for the supply chain'; Element is well positioned across Wafer-Level Packaging and Circuitry. Glass cores seem to be gaining traction based on its R&D and applications development projects; he is not counting on them as a material volume driver in the near term, but 'call it three to five years out, I think it could be quite substantial.'
quarterly_data.figure: could be quite substantial three to five years out (CEO view)

quarterly_data.signal: Micromax: CFO Carey Dorman said Micromax contributed nearly $140 million to reported sales in Q3, roughly 2/3 of it metals, and continues to perform well ahead of plan with significant revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth. CEO Ben Gliklich: Micromax is seeing an uplift in higher-value volume and some decline in lower-value volume that skews towards automotive applications.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly $140 million Q3 sales, roughly 2/3 metals

quarterly_data.signal: Specialties (CFO Carey Dorman): softer Specialty margins came from the offshore customer's equipment failure and price-cost timing in Industrial Solutions, dynamics expected to abate through year-end and into 2027. Industrial Solutions grew 3% organically on price increases tied to raw material inflation (pricing drove about 3%-4% of revenue growth, offsetting almost all of the inflation, with maybe $1 million or $2 million still to pick up); volumes were roughly flat, automotive slightly positive, general industrial and construction down, Asia strong and Europe weak, and he expects more of the same into Q4. Offshore Solutions declined 13% organically on project delays and an equipment failure that shut down a large offshore customer, a few million dollar revenue impact in the quarter; the customer is back online, sales should resume most likely in Q4 with full recovery by Q1 of next year. Element won business on its first, and what it calls the industry's first, deep offshore carbon capture installation, a small contributor today in a nascent market.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial Solutions +3% organic; Offshore Solutions -13% organic; a few million dollar revenue impact

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ben Gliklich: Element and Solstice mutually terminated the proposed transaction at the end of August; while management stands behind its merits, shareholders 'valued the standalone trajectory that we articulated in our May investor day.' Element will keep investing organically and through bolt-on M&A, focused primarily on Electronics assets that consolidate markets or add capabilities; the integrations of Micromax and EFC are going well and both contributed meaningful adjusted EBITDA growth in the quarter. Element is also reorganizing the Electronics segment into more autonomous, customer-aligned business units, all under the MacDermid Alpha brand.

players.product: EFC high-purity specialty gases for satellite propulsion

quarterly_data.signal: EFC Gases and Advanced Materials (CFO Carey Dorman): $23 million of Q3 revenue, a 45% sequential improvement and a 19% increase year-on-year; demand in its core semiconductor manufacturing, satellite and electrical infrastructure applications is strong but lumpier than Element's other businesses, with new business wins at margins above segment averages, growing wallet share with existing semiconductor and space customers and new qualifications in both. Element broke ground on a new EFC facility in Texas late in Q3. CEO Ben Gliklich: big orders are tied to certain satellite launches; the outlook 'is probably better, frankly, based on the pipeline we've seen', and EFC capacity additions contribute to capex in 2026 and into 2027.
